hints: Look at the R-groups given and remember where an enzyme sits: in watery cytoplasm, so which type of R-group would be happy facing water on the outside?
Recall the simple rule: hydrophilic (polar) R-groups face outward to interact with water, while hydrophobic (non-polar) R-groups tuck inward away from water.
walkthrough:
**Picture the enzyme in water**

Enzymes work in the cytoplasm or other watery fluids. So the outside of the protein touches water, while the inside is sheltered away from water.

Think: like dissolves like, water-loving groups want to face water.

**Place the polar histidine**

Histidine has a polar R-group, so it is hydrophilic. Hydrophilic groups form hydrogen bonds with surrounding water.

That means most histidines will be on the surface of the enzyme, facing outward.

**Place the non-polar proline**

Proline has a non-polar R-group, so it is hydrophobic. Hydrophobic groups are repelled by water and cluster together.

That means most prolines will be tucked inside the enzyme, away from water. Surface histidine plus inside proline matches option D.

options.A: This is reversed. Polar histidine would not hide inside away from water, and non-polar proline would not prefer the watery surface.
options.B: Histidine on the surface is correct, but non-polar proline on the surface is wrong because hydrophobic groups avoid contact with water.
options.C: Proline inside is correct, but polar histidine inside is wrong because hydrophilic groups are stable when facing water on the surface.
options.D: Correct. Polar, hydrophilic histidine sits mostly on the surface to interact with water, while non-polar, hydrophobic proline sits mostly inside away from water.
